dossier.public_summary: The dip looks flat-bottomed and planet-sized but alternates between shallow and deep by a factor of three across odd and even events, with only three transits that already show huge depth scatter. That odd-even difference and the sector-to-sector depth change match an eclipsing binary observed at half its true 27.8-day period, not a single planet.

reasons.why: Odd/even depths differ by 3x at high significance, as expected for an eclipsing binary folded at half its true period.
Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent from a planet expectation, with only 3 transits total; the top three carry the whole signal.
Depth appears to change between sectors, and transit_depths shows the same odd/even deep vs shallow pattern, consistent with EB primary/secondary rather than detrending noise alone.
reasons.value: 0.01084 (sector 22 depth_ppm 2061 err 226, sector 72 depth_ppm 3004 err 293, depth_change_pct 37.24)

reasons.why: Implied planet size is small but V shape flagged (fit_b 0.9344, star_density_penalty 4.096) combined with binary indicators positively favors EB over planet; centroid is inconclusive and does not provide counter-evidence.
